source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a repeating process can be used to measure time.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: An old mechanical clock cannot measure time.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A regularly swinging pendulum without a clock face cannot measure time.

intelligence.enrichment: A process can measure time when it repeats continuously after definite intervals, because each repeat can mark an equal interval of time. Regular repetition creates a stable reference interval; counting or comparing those repeats measures elapsed time. The learner correctly applies this rule: A process can measure time when it repeats continuously after definite intervals, because each repeat can mark an equal interval of time. Anything that happens again, such as an irregular drip, can measure time because repetition alone is enough.
